title: Foundations: Neo Soul - The Complete Guide
summary: What Neo Soul is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Neo Soul songs: Neo-soul brought organic musicianship back to R&B: live bands, jazzy chords, and unhurried grooves. D'Angelo, Erykah Badu, and Lauryn Hill made soul thoughtful again in the late 1990s.

History: D'Angelo's Brown Sugar (1995) and Voodoo (2000), Erykah Badu's Baduizm (1997), and Lauryn Hill's Miseducation (1998) defined the movement; the Soulquarians collective was its studio band.

How the songs work: Neo Soul favors the keys of F, Bb, Eb, C. Common forms include Long vamps with improvised vocals; Hip-hop beats under jazz chords. Players should master rhodes electric piano as the core voice first, then behind-the-beat drumming (questlove's dilla feel). Rhodes piano territory.

title: Neo Soul Etude No. 1: Voodoo ii–V–I
summary: An original Neo Soul study in Bb drilling behind-the-beat drumming (questlove's dilla feel).
body:
This original etude isolates the 'Voodoo ii–V–I' progression in the key of Bb — the changes Neo Soul players must know cold.

CHART:

title: Untitled (How Does It Feel) - Neo Soul Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Untitled (How Does It Feel) by D'Angelo (2000).
body:
Untitled (How Does It Feel) — D'Angelo, 2000. The Voodoo slow-burn; the iconic video.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of Eb):
D# | Cm | Fm | A#7

This study chart uses the 'Badu I–vi–ii–V' progression, the Neo Soul workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: long vamps with improvised vocals. Listen for unresolved jazzy chord voicings — it is the fingerprint of the style.
